amendments.summary: Gov't Code 3000.002 (HB 2439, 86R, eff. 2019-09-01): a governmental entity may not adopt or enforce a rule/ordinance/building code that prohibits or limits a building product, material or method approved by a national model code published within the last three code cycles, or sets a standard stricter than that code. Local code amendments are allowed only if they do not conflict. Exceptions include areas of historical/cultural/architectural significance where the city is a Certified Local Government or has a THC-compliant landmark ordinance (and designations made by April 1, 2019 / National Register districts), and state-agency programs. SB 783 (2025) amended ch. 3000 to exempt SECO-adopted energy codes. Private deed restrictions/HOAs are not reached.

Keystone metro cost factor (BLS OEWS wages, see README cost method)

factor.note: No metro wage data for this place (non-metro or not in table); Texas statewide factor used.

cost.method: Factor = 0.40*L + 0.60*M, rounded to 2 decimals. L = weighted mean of (metro annual median wage / US national annual median wage) for SOC 47-2031 Carpenters (0.30), 47-2111 Electricians (0.20), 47-2152 Plumbers/Pipefitters/Steamfitters (0.20), 47-2061 Construction Laborers (0.20), 49-9021 HVAC Mechanics/Installers (0.10), from BLS OEWS; weights renormalised over occupations available for the MSA. M = materials index, 1.00 for all Texas metros (no public citable reason to adjust); qualitative materials notes per MSA. Wave 2 (2026-10-11): all five trades retrieved from O*NET Texas local-wages pages (OEWS May 2024) via search extracts (Secondary); HVAC missing for 28660, 47380, 46340, 17780 (weights renormalised there). provisional removed for every MSA with >=4 trades.

plainLanguage: Texas sets a minimum house code (the 2012 IRC) but most cities use the newer 2021 IRC with local changes - always confirm with your city. The statewide energy code is still the 2015 IRC energy chapter; a newer one is under state review. Your county sets your climate zone; under the newer 2021 energy code Dallas and Tarrant counties count as a warmer zone (2A) than Collin or Denton (3A). Electrical work follows the 2026 National Electrical Code for permits filed from Sept 1, 2026. Cities cannot require fire sprinklers in a house, and generally cannot require brick or stone - but your HOA, deed restrictions or a historic district can. On the coast you need a TDI windstorm certificate; homes started from April 1, 2026 are checked against the 2024 IRC wind rules. In big cities, a 2025 law (SB 15) lets new subdivisions have small lots (down to 3,000 sq ft) with small setbacks. Much of Texas has shrink-swell clay, so plan on an engineer-designed slab.
